title: Surgeons Should Not Look like Surgeons
coreMove: Look past polished signals and ask which evidence actually connects the person to successful performance under risk.
sourcePressure: Professional theater can mislead trust when appearance becomes a substitute for competence under consequence.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making it about sloppy dress versus polished dress instead of cosmetic signal versus tested competence.

sourceAnchors.name: Surgeons Should Not Look like Surgeons
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen title and sidecar support a chapter about distrust of theatrical expertise markers and preference for practical credibility.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The surgeon image works when it tests a trust shortcut: the costume can calm you while telling you almost nothing about the hand holding the scalpel.
